challenge.title: Government and Community Evidence Challenge
challenge.description: Complete 10 activities: six supporting-clue and conclusion decisions, then four matching tasks. Both parts of an evidence decision count together as one activity. Get at least 7 activities correct to pass. All lesson clues are available even without saving them in your journal.

badge.name: Government and Community Investigator
badge.description: Earned by completing all four Chapter 7 missions and passing the evidence challenge. Recognizes careful explanations of offices, tribute, settlement changes and community experiences.

evidence.question: A caption says the colonial governor-general was a modern elected Philippine president. Which clue directly checks this substitution, and what conclusion fits?
choices: The governor-general was a colonial office, not the modern elected presidency
Every historical office is identical to a modern position
Every local community elected that official under modern rules
The governor-general had no relationship with the monarchy
evidence.explanation: The modern-substitution clue explicitly distinguishes the colonial governor-general from a modern elected presidency. A petition or payment form does not establish that office's relationship to modern government.

evidence.question: A report says a duty was always fulfilled fairly because it appears in the office description. Choose the clue that checks this claim and its supported conclusion.
choices: A responsibility still needs evidence of actions and consequences
Listing a duty proves universal fair performance
A title tells every resident's feelings
The officeholder performed every task alone
evidence.explanation: The duty-versus-performance clue requires evidence of actions and consequences. Provincial titles and the definition of settlement policy cannot demonstrate that a particular duty was fairly fulfilled.

evidence.question: A town petition requests change, but no decision is supplied. Which clue directly checks a claim that the petition succeeded?
choices: The request is evidence of an attempt, not proof of its outcome
Every recorded request was granted
A petition reveals every resident's consent
No reply means no one made a request
evidence.explanation: The recorded-request clue separates an attempt to seek a decision from a successful result. A court's functions or the title encomendero does not provide the missing reply.

evidence.question: An exhibit treats an encomienda grant as automatic ownership of every field. Choose the direct clue and the supported conclusion.
choices: Collection rights do not automatically establish land ownership; land claims need their own evidence
Every grant automatically transferred all fields and residents as property
An encomienda was simply a voluntary gift
A collection record settles every land dispute
evidence.explanation: The separate-land-question clue distinguishes collection rights from automatic ownership. Issuing an order or describing an administrative aim cannot settle the land claim.

evidence.question: An account says tribute was a voluntary present because its label sounds favorable. Which clue directly checks that claim?
choices: Tribute was required under authority, not automatically a freely offered gift
Every payment was freely chosen by all households
One label proves every payment amount was identical
A favorable description establishes universal consent
evidence.explanation: The requirement clue identifies tribute as a required payment. Earlier leadership and a separate petition do not change that distinction into a voluntary gift.

evidence.question: A proposed town layout is offered as proof of everything built and occupied. Which clue directly tests that inference?
choices: Design instructions and actual building or residence evidence are different
Every prescribed building was necessarily built and occupied
A proposed layout reveals every household's feelings
The diagram gives exact travel times for all families
evidence.explanation: The prescription-and-practice clue separates design rules from what was built or occupied. Defense responsibilities or a town title cannot establish implementation of the plan.

matching.question: Match each stage of an order with the evidence question it raises.
pairs: Did the message reach the particular place?
What was put into practice and how did people respond?
matching.explanation: A recorded decision, its delivery and its implementation are distinct. Evidence of one stage does not guarantee every later effect.

matching.question: Match each local-government idea with its careful description.
pairs: A town-level colonial office, distinct from governor-general
Prominent local participants, not every Indigenous person
Some influence could persist while institutional relationships changed
matching.explanation: Keep offices and social roles in historical context. A local title does not make all people the same or establish every resident's experience.

matching.question: Match the record type with the question it most directly helps investigate.
pairs: What collection rights and duties were stated?
What payments or goods were recorded as received?
What problem or disputed practice was raised?
matching.explanation: These records can support different parts of the inquiry. None alone establishes every land claim, fair performance or a complaint's final outcome.

matching.question: Match the settlement evidence with what it can establish most directly.
pairs: What an authority wanted people to do
How a settlement was intended to be arranged
Where people actually lived in a particular setting
matching.explanation: Policy and design are not the same as implementation. Residence, daily effects and local responses still need evidence for the particular place and period.
